To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the P/C mRNA uses a ribosomal shunting mechanism to initiate translation of the Y1/Y2 proteins.
the Sendai virus P mRNA uses a ribosomal shunting mechanism to translate the Y1 and the Y2 proteins.
ribosomal shunting is used to initiate translation of the C-terminal ORFs in the P/C mRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of initiation of the P and Y proteins of Sendai virus, which are expressed by a combination of cotranscriptional editing of the P/C mRNA and ribosome shunting.
the mechanism of ribosomal initiation from the P/C mRNA of Sendai virus, an orthomyxovirus that is the prototype of the Paramyxoviridae family.
how the ribosome is able to recognize and translate the Y1 and the Y2 proteins, which have no known homologs in the viral or host genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Y proteins are expressed by a combination of ribosome shunting and leaky scanning.
the Y proteins are translated via a ribosomal scanning shunt.
the Sendai virus Y proteins are initiated by a ribosomal shunting mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Sendai virus P mRNA is translated by a combination of leaky scanning and a ribosomal shunting mechanism.
the Sendai virus P mRNA is transcribed by the host cell RNA polymerase II, and the primary transcript is processed by host cell enzymes to produce a capped, polyadenylated mRNA.
ribosomal choice and shunting account for the expression of the Sendai virus P and Y proteins, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ribosomal shunt can be an important mechanism of translation initiation.
ribosomal scanning can be discontinuous and can occur in a cap-dependent manner.
the P/C mRNA uses a novel mechanism to translate its +1 ORF.
